newsitem.title: USA: American Home says panel views vaccine safe. [CORRECTED 23:13 GMT]
newsitem.headline: American Home says panel views vaccine safe. [CORRECTED 23:13 GMT]

text.p: American Home Products Corp said a U.S. Food and Drug Administration advisory panel determined that its Acel-Imune vaccine was safe and effective when given to infants.

The company said the advisory panel concluded on Tuesday the diphtheria and tetanus toxoids and acellular pertussis vaccine was safe and effective as a primary series at two, four, and six months of age and as a fourth dose given at about 18 months.
A final decision by the FDA on whether to grant marketing approval for use of the vaccine in infants is pending.

"We are committed to working with the FDA to finalize the licensure of this vaccine for the full five-dose diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis immunization series," Ronald Saldarini, president of American Home's Wyeth-Lederle Vaccines and Pediatrics unit, said in a statement.

The vaccine was first approved by the FDA in 1991 and is indicated for the fourth and fifth doses in older children who have received whole-cell diptheria, tetanus and pertussis vaccine for the first three doses.

Separately North American Vaccine Inc said the anel concluded its diphtheria, tetanus and acellular pertussis vaccine, Certiva, is safe and effective for administration in infants at two, four, six and 15-18 months of age.

The FDA committee "raised no concerns" regarding the adequacy of the data on the use of Certiva for the booster dose given to children at four-to-six years following primary immunization using the whole-cell pertussis vaccine, North American Vaccine said.

Nonetheless, the company's stock was off 2-7/8 to 21-3/8 on Wednesday. Sharon Mates, North American Vaccine's president, attributed the drop to negative interpretations of the FDA panel meeting. But she the vaccine was advancing in the approval process.
"We're moving along with the FDA, everything is moving along," Mates said in an interview.

In July the FDA approved an acellular pertussis vaccine made by the Connaught Laboratories unit of Rhone-Poulenc SA and an FDA advisory panel recommended approval of a SmithKline Beecham Plc diptheria, tetanus and pertussis vaccine. (Corrects to make clear that it was a panel recommendation for the SmithKline vaccine).
